chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
Take the pebbles for the Jamarah from Jam', and if you take them from your place of departure in Mina, it will suffice you.
ai.seo_question: Where should the pebbles for Jamarat be taken from during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility in sourcing pebbles for the Ramy al-Jamarat, affirming that while collecting them from Jam' (Muzdalifah) is the normative practice, taking them from one's saddle in Mina remains legally valid (mufeed). This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the permissibility of alternative sources when the primary method is difficult, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Hajj rituals. It highlights the distinction between the recommended act (mustahabb) and the sufficient act (ja'iz) in Shia fiqh.
